Q: Why is it allowed to pass the parameter value by reference with the duplicated sign &? A:

A deref coercion automatically converts values of type &Tto values of type &U where T implements Deref<Target = U>.

In-particular, there is a blanket implementation impl<T> Deref for &T where T: ?Sized, which sets Target = T;. So deref coercions can remove extra references.

Q: What do spaCy's part-of-speech and dependency tags mean? A:

spaCy uses Universal Dependencies annotations for token.pos_ and token.dep_:

  • for .pos_ (parts of speech, English): https://universaldependencies.org/u/pos/

  • for .dep_ (dependency relations, English): https://universaldependencies.org/u/dep/

While for the finer-grained parts of speech in English, it uses the Penn Treebank annotations, which should also map onto the coarse-grained Universal POS.

Q: Scan directories and copy those that have more than n files A: 
from pathlib import Path
import shutil


SOURCE = Path('music')
DEST = Path('musiclight')
MIN_SONGS = 7


# Create destination directory if it doesn't exist
DEST.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


# Process each artist
for artist in SOURCE.iterdir():

    # Skip files; we only want artist directories
    if not artist.is_dir():
        continue

    # Count all files recursively inside the artist directory
    count = sum(
        1
        for file in artist.rglob('*')
        if file.is_file()
    )

    print(f'{artist.name}: {count} songs')

    # Copy artist if they have enough songs
    if count >= MIN_SONGS:
        shutil.copytree(
            artist,
            DEST / artist.name,
            dirs_exist_ok=True
        )

Q: No module named uvicorn when debugging through vscode A:

Are you using a Python package manager like uv?

If so, you have to use it in order to run your app. uv creates it's own venv managed environment, so to use those dependencies you have to run commands through uv.

You'd have to do something like:

{
    "version": "0.2.0",
    "configurations": [
        {
            "name": "Python: FastAPI (UV)",
            "type": "python",
            "request": "launch",
            "program": "${workspaceFolder}/.venv/bin/uv",   // path to the uv binary
            "args": [
                "run",
                "uvicorn",
                "api.main:app",
                "--reload",              // optional: hot reload
                "--host", "0.0.0.0",
                "--port", "8000"
            ],
            "console": "integratedTerminal",
            "justMyCode": true
        }
    ]
}

Q: MySQL ERROR 2013 (HY000): Lost connection to MySQL server during query A:

Problem solved, although without knowing exactly what caused it. I uninstalled the MySQL server completely, deleted all the tables, reinstalled the server, re-initialised it, and restored the database dump. This time, the restore was successful. I assume, as @LSemi suggested, that there was corruption in the InnoDB tablespace.

Q: Sparse checkout but exclude or ignore files in root? A:

It's possible to use the --no-cone option with git sparse-checkout set to only checkout the wanted path, meanwhile excluding all other files in a sparse checkout:

# 1. create the initial sparse clone
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse <repo/url>

# cd /path/to/repo

# 2. use '--no-cone' to exclude everything but the wanted dir
git sparse-checkout set --no-cone "/wanted_dir/"

With that the root files checked out from step 1 would be removed upon step 2.

See https://git-scm.com/docs/git-sparse-checkout#Documentation/git-sparse-checkout.txt-set
